Title: IHD and partners launch Malezi Bora Initiative
NewsSummary: Project aims at promoting use of routine health services for mother and child
NewsContent:
Aga Khan University's Institute for Human Development (IHD) and its private and public sector partners have launched the the Malezi Bora 2018 Initiative which aims to promote the use of routine health services by mothers and children living in Nairobi County.

IHD has partnered with Aga Khan Foundation (AKF), AKF's community partner, Daraja Civic Initiatives Forum (CIF), Kidogo and the Nairobi County to launch the initiative that seeks to scale up sustainable, affordable and high quality models for early childhood services. The event, which took place at Trinity Daycare Centre in Ruaraka in Nairobi County, advocates for the use of routine health services for mother and child in all health services within the crucial, first 1,000 days of a child's life. The daycare centre is one of the projects under Building Brighter Futures and hosts over 110 children aged six months to six years. 

Speaking at the launch, Nairobi's County Deputy Director of Education Peter Miano highlighted the importance of a healthy lifestyle for early childhood development and use of routine health services by mothers, caregivers and families for children's benefit. 

"Teachers, parents and caregivers have a collective responsibility to ensure children are healthy. When a child is not healthy, their learning cycle gets affected," said Dr Kofi Marfo, IHD's director. "The launch is a great highlight and exposure for the vulnerable group (under 4ss) and a demonstration of a sustainability plan for the Building Brighter Futures project that just concluded and this partnership project looks to build strong foundations for children in informal settlements."

Trinity Daycare founder and caregiver Elizabeth Omollo lauded the County's involvement in the initiative. 

"We congratulate you for nurturing care for young children, linking families and children to maternal and child health services at our facilities through community health volunteers," Ms Omollo added.

Launched in 2007, the Building Brighter Futures project covers Babadogo, Kibera, Kangemi Mathare, Githurai and Kawangware amongst other areas.
